newsitem.title: USA: Heat buoys U.S. spot resids despite crude slide.
newsitem.headline: Heat buoys U.S. spot resids despite crude slide.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Monday in thin trade, with scorching heat along the East Coast supporting values despite a softer crude market, industry sources said.
"With the heat and some record generation demand, we could see a little upside (in prices), but I don't see it going far," said one East Coast utility source, noting gas was still cheaper than resid.
Heat and humidity are expected to plague the East this week though levels should moderate some from today's mid-90s F later in the week.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped slightly to the $16.50 a barrel area, with August one percent paper off 10-20 cents to $16.05-20 on softer crude.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was unchanged at $17.75, while high sulphurs in New York also held steady, with 2.2 percent still pegged in the low-$15s.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent remained in the low-$16s, while three percent held at $14.25-50, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices firmed at least a nickel Monday to the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu or higher, or $15.50 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was up a couple of cents to $2.18/mmBtu, or $13.73 a barrel.
